response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS vol FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, vol, vol / (SELECT SUM(vol) FROM p) AS share FROM p), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.vol) AS combined_order_volume, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Order volume means the total quantity ordered, i.e. SUM of product_quantity (a VARCHAR, cast to a number) per product in Order_Items; share = product's quantity / total quantity across all order items.
The plain average of shares is taken over products that appear in Order_Items (products never ordered are not included).
The result is a single unrounded row: combined quantity of above-average products, their mean share, and their mean (share minus the overall average share).

alternatives.interpretation: Order volume means the number of order item rows per product (count of order lines), ignoring the quantity column.
alternatives.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) * 1.0 AS vol FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, vol, vol / (SELECT SUM(vol) FROM p) AS share FROM p), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.vol) AS combined_order_volume, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
